public_rationale: The August 19, 2023 demonstrations document recurring GPT-3.5 rule violations, including attempts to capture its own queen and move a rook through its own pawn despite specialized prompting [e1]. The same report includes complete legal GPT-4 games [e1]. A July 29 demonstration, outside the August 1–20 target window, also records a legal 38-move GPT-4 game and a prompt-dependent illegal move [e2]. The August evidence supports unreliable rule adherence, while its successful games rule out categorical inability to play legally [e1].
limitations: The demonstrations do not establish a representative failure rate or cover every LLM [e1, e2].
They do not test the separate comparison with humans learning unfamiliar rules from modest instruction [e1, e2].
Support depends on interpreting the claim as unreliable adherence rather than inability to follow any rules [e1].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLMs cannot stick to explicit rules such as the rules of chess.

statement.excerpt: Humans can learn rules of games like chess from modest amounts of explicit instruction; LLMs can’t stick to explicit rules.
statement.document_title: No, Virginia, AGI is not imminent

from_speaker: Humans can learn rules of games like chess
LLMs can’t stick to explicit rules
our_interpretation: The plain reading is a criticism of dependable rule adherence over an interaction, not a claim that LLMs never produce legal moves.
Chess provides the concrete test: making legal moves throughout games when asked to play, without an external engine enforcing legality.

For this ongoing observation, I use August 2023 through publication as the latest reporting window. The monthly boundary is an evaluator convention because model evaluations have no fixed reporting cycle.
The normalized proposition concerns LLM rule adherence. The separate claim about how quickly humans learn is not established by chess transcripts alone.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous tests show recurring violations of game rules or explicit interaction instructions despite clear requests to play, including failures beyond isolated notation mistakes.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Contemporaneous, repeated tests show dependable adherence throughout varied games and explicitly specified rule tasks under modest instruction.
